subject.title: Exec provider: 1Password op CLI spawns daemon processes, hangs on macOS Tahoe (needs --cache=false)

question: Should OpenClaw handle the 1Password CLI cache-daemon problem as docs/doctor guidance on the existing exec-provider surface, a generic exec-provider runtime contract, or an `op`-specific runtime special case?
rationale: The issue affects secret-provider startup and service-account handling, but root policy keeps core lean and avoids owner-specific behavior when existing config, docs, doctor, or plugin surfaces are adequate.

options.title: Document and diagnose existing workaround
options.body: Add public docs and possibly doctor/troubleshooting guidance for `env: { OP_CACHE: "false" }` or prepended `--cache=false` without changing runtime command behavior.

options.title: Design a generic exec safety contract
options.body: Add a non-1Password-specific provider contract only after maintainers define compatibility, security, and validation expectations for side-effecting secret CLIs.

options.title: Special-case 1Password in runtime
options.body: Auto-inject `OP_CACHE=false` or prepend `--cache=false` for `op`, accepting a core vendor-specific policy branch.

recommendation.title: Document and diagnose existing workaround
recommendation.body: Add public docs and possibly doctor/troubleshooting guidance for `env: { OP_CACHE: "false" }` or prepended `--cache=false` without changing runtime command behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh authored the core exec SecretRef baseline and eager runtime activation path, making him the strongest history-backed owner for the contract decision.
